title: Building an Autonomous Engineering Org - Angie Jones, Agentic AI Foundation
talk_summary: Angie Jones describes Block's path from IDE autocomplete to agents that take tickets end-to-end, driven by a hand-picked 'AI champions' group that made repos AI-ready (context/rules files, slash commands, AI review) before scaling delegation. The concrete mechanisms are repo-level context assets, ticket/Slack-native delegation, bot PR review with an auto-fix loop, and isolated cloud workspaces per parallel agent.

takeaways.technique: Repo-readiness assets as the prerequisite for delegation
takeaways.what_they_do: Before expecting agents to produce mergeable PRs, champions added agents.md/claude.md context files, rules files for guardrails, and repeatable slash-command workflows inside each repo, customized per repo shape rather than mandated top-down.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they added assets like contacts and rules files so that agents could reliably understand and navigate the code base
takeaways.numbers: AI-authored code up 69%, reported time savings +37%, automated PRs up 21x after 3 months

takeaways.technique: Bot review plus automatic fix loop before human review
takeaways.what_they_do: They made AI code review mandatory on all repos and wired a second agent that automatically fixes issues the reviewer flags and commits to the same PR, so humans only see cleaned-up PRs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we also created an auto-fix loop where if Codex identified issues, another agent will automatically fix those issues and commit them to the PR

takeaways.technique: Delegation from where work already lives (tickets, GitHub issues, chat)
takeaways.what_they_do: Agents are assignable directly from Jira/Linear tickets, GitHub issues, and Slack mentions, so delegation feels native and non-champions don't learn a new tool.
takeaways.evidence_quote: all engineers didn't necessarily have to learn a new skill. The champions had already laid the foundation
takeaways.numbers: Slack bug-to-PR cycle cited as ~5 minutes

takeaways.technique: Isolated cloud workspace per parallel agent
takeaways.what_they_do: When parallel agents exhausted laptops (OOM, CPU), they moved each agent into its own dedicated cloud workspace so runs are isolated and can execute anywhere.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we invested in dedicated cloud workspaces where each agent ran in its own isolated environment

takeaways.technique: Machine-readable system map for cross-repo planning
takeaways.what_they_do: They built a 'company world model' of all repos and service dependencies so orchestrators and sub-agents can pull context and plan changes spanning multiple codebases in parallel.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a machine-readable view of every single service and how they all connect

takeaways.technique: Champions program to seed patterns, not top-down mandate
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of leveling up everyone, they picked ~50 engineers (~1%) from critical teams, gave them 30% time, and let them define per-repo patterns that then spread to similar teams.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I decided to focus on forming the 1%, the power users, from our most critical teams
